idiom_name: async handler function + sqlx Transaction with ? propagation and drop-rollback
implementation_notes: Rust has no class-per-script convention: the script is an async function (usually an axum/actix handler or a service method) that acquires a transaction with pool.begin().await? and runs its queries through &mut *tx, propagating every failure with ?. sqlx supplies RAII semantics - a Transaction still in progress when it goes out of scope is rolled back on drop - so the rollback path needs no explicit code, while commit() consumes the transaction and must be the last fallible step. Presentation stays outside: the handler returns Result<Json<T>, AppError> and the script is a plain async function over the pool, which makes it testable against a scratch database. Diesel's connection.transaction(|conn| ...) closure is the blocking equivalent with the same commit-on-Ok/rollback-on-Err contract.
pitfalls: Returning Err before commit() is safe only because Drop rolls back - but a failed commit must still be propagated, or the outcome is silently unknown.
The transaction borrows a pooled connection for its whole lifetime; a forgotten .await or blocking work between begin and commit can exhaust the pool.
Holding the transaction across a long side effect (HTTP call, message send) keeps row locks; keep side effects after commit or use an outbox.
